name: Duck Meat
description: Duck meat (Anas platyrhynchos) consists of high-density dark muscle fibers characterized by a unique lipid-protein architecture. Unlike typical avian poultry, duck muscle possesses a higher concentration of myoglobin and heme-iron, providing a substrate profile closer to red meat. This food matrix serves as a robust source of structural amino acids and B-complex coenzymes, essential for oxidative energy production, hemoglobin stabilization, and systemic maintenance of neural and immune integrity.
macroTitle: Macro Nutrients (per 100g, raw meat without skin)
macroIntro: A protein-dense muscular matrix distinguished by total lack of glycemic substrate and an optimal monounsaturated lipid profile.
microIntro: A highly bioavailable repository of heme-iron, zinc, and B-complex vitamins, critical for cellular respiration and metabolic signaling.

microNutrients.name: Zinc

microNutrients.description: Critical substrate for fatty acid synthesis and adrenal hormone regulation under metabolic stress.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B12
microNutrients.description: Essential for myelin sheath maintenance and preventing the maturation arrest of erythrocytes.

healthBenefits: Optimized Oxygen Kinetics: High heme iron density paired with B12 dramatically enhances erythropoiesis and tissue oxygen delivery.
Mitochondrial Energetic Resilience: Abundant B3 and B5 concentrations accelerate ATP synthesis pathways, reducing functional metabolic fatigue.
Immunological Signal Boosting: High concentrations of zinc and selenium amplify the efficiency of leukocyte cellular responses.
Structural Protein Synthesis: A pristine amino acid architecture facilitates immediate repair and growth of skeletal muscle fibers.
precautionsIntro: While skinless duck meat is a lean nutrient source, the inclusion of subcutaneous fat depots necessitates careful preparation:
precautions: Caloric and Lipid Overload: Retention of skin/fat layers significantly increases the saturated fat concentration, requiring strict quantitative intake monitoring.
Microbiological Pathogen Exposure: Like all poultry, potential Campylobacter and Salmonella presence mandates thermal sterilization at an internal core of 74C.
Purine Metabolism Considerations: Elevated purine content may precipitate hyperuricemia in susceptible phenotypes; portions should be managed in individuals with diagnosed gout.
